rule: No blanket policies. All 23 application tables remain RLS-enabled with zero policies because browser roles receive no direct table privileges after the targeted Stage 5 revoke. Business access is intentionally mediated through issuer-gated Better Auth RPCs, validated participant portal token RPCs, public read/event RPCs, or service_role-only backend paths. Platform auth/storage tables remain out of scope.

positive owner/role/token tests through the supported RPC/Edge boundary

checks: All 23 application-owned tables exist, remain owned by postgres, retain RLS, and have zero policies.
anon and authenticated have no effective SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, REFERENCES, TRIGGER or MAINTAIN privilege on the 23 tables.
No explicit PUBLIC ACL remains on the 23 application tables.
service_role retains CRUD on the 20 designated public backend tables and has no direct table grants on the three private tables.
The direct table checks ran after Stage 5 ACL revoke and the Stage 7 portal/password/legacy-certificate hardening on the disposable restore.
limitations: This acceptance covers direct table RLS/ACL boundaries only; it does not replace the separate SECURITY DEFINER caller/issuer/token audit, which is tracked per table.
No Production grants, policies, DDL, DML, user rows or account changes are included.

notes: The five chat_group tables retain RLS enabled, zero policies, and no direct browser table privileges.

The retirement migration revokes PUBLIC/anon/authenticated table privileges, revokes EXECUTE on public/private chat RPCs, removes chat-named Realtime tables, and retains table rows for controlled archival.
The only remaining non-chat caller is admin_force_delete_competition on chat_groups; its legacy-issuer denial and Better Auth admin path are tested separately.

The three private organizer/referral tables remain RLS-enabled with zero policies, no direct grants to browser or service_role, and no private schema USAGE/CREATE for anon/authenticated/service_role. They are reachable only from Better Auth issuer/identity-guarded owner/admin RPCs, the server-only Better Auth provisioning routine, or internal trigger functions. The legacy auth.users signup/referral triggers are dropped in the identity-root draft.

The two public Shop promo banner tables remain RLS-enabled with zero policies and no direct anon/authenticated table grants. Anonymous storefront access is limited to active-banner listing and a validated, deduplicated VIEW/CLICK RPC; raw banner/event rows stay service_role-only. Banner Admin CRUD is exposed only through authenticated Admin SECURITY DEFINER RPCs, whose shared role helper verifies the exact Better Auth issuer and private.app_users identity_origin.

competition_status_history has no direct browser grants. Better Auth owner/Admin transition RPC writes history; the public results RPC reads only RESULT_PUBLISHED history for PUBLIC competitions after publication; the Admin monitoring RPC has an issuer-gated Admin boundary; the status trigger is not directly executable by browser roles.

Baseline #364 (commit b7a28adc) passed all 75 numbered workflow steps plus post-job cleanup. Its disposable-restore acceptance closes the three server-authoritative exam tables, including cross-participant token IDOR, result publication projection and parent/child session revocation.

notification_deliveries has no database or Realtime caller; supabase_system_logs has one exact postgres-owned service_role-only collector. Both boundaries passed the latest disposable runtime ACL/caller scan.
The remaining four pending tables are payment_gateway_configs, payment_gateway_state, shop_user_vouchers and shop_voucher_definitions; their SECURITY DEFINER owner/issuer paths are the next tranche.
